President’s Column
Art Liestman
Ken Vicketts of Lee Valley gave an informative
and detailed presentation on pen turning at the
February meeting. Ken was called upon at the
last minute to fill in for Kathy Somerville who
was unable to make it to the meeting. Ken’s
presentation was so fascinating that nobody felt
they could do it justice in these pages.
Hopefully, we’ll have an article on pens in the
near future.
Sandy Dougal volunteered to help out with the
instant gallery. In the future, when you submit
your piece to the gallery, please indicate if you
would like a critique of the work. A critique
will only be offered for those submissions for
which it is requested.
We modified the schedule for the last meeting,
moving the “wood exchange” to the end of the
meeting so as not to cut the speaker short. We
try to squeeze as much as possible into our
meetings. If you have any suggestions about
how to do it more smoothly, please let us know.
We (the executive, that is) are always interested
in ways to improve our meetings, so please
don’t be shy in making suggestions or giving us
feedback.
Thanks to Paul Grant for providing the photos
this month!

Dougal showed off his skills with a maple burl
and inlay bowl. Bill Luck's fir burl bowl was
impressive. Les Crossley displayed an
ingenious multi-sectioned adjustable floor lamp.
Don Hoskins presented a turned and then carved
cherry vase that appeared to be entwined ivy
leaves. Cornelius Regehr showed an elegant
maple burl bowl. Thanks for your participation.
The February President’s challenge was indeed
challenging - to make a pair of identical items.
Unfortunately, this may have been the cause of
a smaller than usual turnout. Phil Laliberte,
never one to shy away from a challenge, showed
a pair of Honduran pine goblets. (Well, one of
them was actually a scoop, illustrating one of
the pitfalls of such a challenge.) Bruce
Campbell made a pair of lamps (of laminated
walnut and birch). Ken Booth brought a pair of
spurtles (Scottish kitchen implements which the
President preferred to think of as drum sticks).
Mike Dawson displayed a pair of tiny goblets
with captive rings. David MacDonald made a
nice pair of knitting spools. (It's great to see the
younger members participating!) Finally, Less
Crossley showed a pair of glasses. Thanks to
the participants of this month’s President’s
Challenge.
Don’t forget your toothpaste tube rollers for the
March challenge!

Vancouver Woodturners Guild, an election of
executive officers took place at the February

chairperson of the nominating committee,
chaired this part of the meeting.
Elected to a two-year term were Art Liestman as
president and Dave Martin as secretary. The
following members were elected to one-year

The decision was made to elect these officers to
one- year terms at this time so only part of the
executive will change annually. In February
2001, members running for the positions of
vice-president, treasurer, and member at large
will be elected for a two-year term. Hopefully
this plan will ensure continuity.
As there was an overwhelming number of
volunteers for the positions, Andrew Forrest
was added as a second member at large. One of
Andrew’s special responsibilities will be to fill
in for executive members who are unable to
attend meetings. We welcome Andrew as a new
member of the executive.
Members who are interested in discovering what
really happens at executive meetings are
welcome to attend. Executive meetings, when
required, are generally held on the second
Monday of the month at ARC Arts Council
building, 2425 St. Johns Street, in Port Moody.
As meetings do not take place every month, you
are advised to check with a member of the
executive before deciding to attend.
Secretary’s Report
Dave Martin
The Greater Vancouver Woodturners Guild now
has sixty-five members who come from
seventeen different communities in the Lower
Mainland. Almost forty percent of our
members are from Coquitlam and Surrey with a
further twenty percent from Vancouver and
Burnaby. Robert Prinse and Cornelius Regehr
from Chilliwack along with Terry Allen from
Sardis have the farthest distance to travel.
In many ways our group is quite diverse. Some
of our members have been turning wood for
many years while others have yet to buy their
first lathe. Our group also covers a wide age
range. Several of our members are secondary
school students while a number of others are
enjoying their retirement years. In other
respects, however, we are certainly lacking in
diversity as only two of our sixty-five members
are women. We do welcome Amie Hillaby and
Janis Horne and assure other female
woodturners that they are most welcome.
One of the most remarkable statistics for our
group is the fact that about fifty woodturners or
eighty percent of our members attend each
meeting! Thanks for attending and for keeping
our meetings interesting.
All members are reminded that our membership
year is from September to September.

Bonnie Klein Visits the GVWG!
Art Liestman
We are very excited about the upcoming visit by
Bonnie Klein. Bonnie is a full-time woodturner
based near Seattle, specializing in small-scale
woodturnings such as tops, pens, earrings, and
lidded boxes. She designed and produces the
Klein Designs lathe that is specially made for
such small-scale work. She also produced a
comprehensive set of instructional videos that
show the great range of work that can be done
on a small lathe. She is particularly active
among woodturning guilds and has served on
the AAW’s Board of Directors and as the VicePresident of the AAW.
Bonnie is much in demand as a teacher of
woodturning and teaches regularly in North
America, Europe, and Australia. In addition to
her detailed technical knowledge, she is highly
creative and always seeking to improve and
progress. Her enthusiasm is addictive. Every
member of the guild of any skill level can learn
from her and be inspired to new heights. We
are very fortunate to have Bonnie as our guild’s
first special visitor. Everyone is strongly
encouraged to attend the events. You will not
regret it!
Bonnie will give a 2 hour seminar and
demonstration at 7:30 pm on Friday, April 14th.
In addition, she will teach two hands-on classes
from 9am to 4pm, on both Saturday, April 15th
and Sunday, April 16th. All of the events will be
held in the Belcarra Hall (see directions below,
thanks to Don Hoskins).
The charge for the seminar is $20 if you pay at
the March meeting or $25 at the door. We’d
like to encourage spouses or children to attend,
so we will ask only $10 for each additional
family member. The classes will be $110 per
student per day with all materials, tools, and
lathes supplied. Classes are limited to a
maximum of 8 students per day. There are still a
couple of spaces left in the Sunday class. See
Don Hoskins at the March meeting to sign up
for the remaining spaces.
To avoid lineups and delays at the actual events,
please give a cheque made out to Greater
Vancouver Woodturners Guild for the
appropriate amount to Don Hoskins at the
March meeting.
The Belcarra Hall is located at 4084 Bedwell
Bay Road in the village of Belcarra. Bedwell
Bay Road is the main road into the village.
To get to Belcarra, first go to the intersection of
the Barnet Highway and Ioco Road in Port
Moody. Belcarra is about a 15 minute drive
from that intersection.
From Vancouver take the Barnet Highway #7A
through Port Moody to Ioco Road. Turn left
(north). Since Lougheed is under construction
for Sky Train between Gaglardi Way and North
Road, if you come from Vancouver, take the
Freeway and turn north on Gaglardi Way.
Drive past Lougheed to Broadway (second light
after Lougheed). Turn right on Broadway and
then turn left at Clarke Road (the second light).
Follow this road which eventually joins the
Barnet Highway in Port Moody. Proceed to
Ioco Road and turn left (north).
If you are coming from the Port Mann Bridge
take the Lougheed Highway #7 to the Barnet
Highway. Turn left (west) onto the Barnet

Once you are heading north on Ioco Road, turn

Regional News
Art Liestman
The Northwest Washington Woodturners (the
nearest AAW chapter to us) is participating in
Woodfest in Sedro Wooley, Washington on
April 8th and 9th. The NWW will have a booth
featuring their work and will be doing live
demonstrations. There will also be displays of
the work of furniture makers and crafts people
from the area. If you have some time free on
that weekend, it is worth the trip.
You are also reminded that the Pacific
Northwest Turning Symposium is to be held
May 4 - 6 in Everett, Washington at the Howard
Johnson Plaza Hotel and Convention Center.
Some details were in last month’s newsletter
and we should be receiving an update in the
mail soon from the organizers. If you put your
name on their list, you should be receiving it at
the same time. If you didn’t get on the list, you
can contact Earl St. Clair, Puget Sound
Woodworking Center, 2416 California Street,
Everett, WA 98201.
Canadian Woodturning Competition
Art Liestman
The GVWG has been asked to take over the
organization of the Canadian Woodturning
Competition that has been run for the past three
years by the Fraser Valley Woodturners. This
competition is held at the Surrey Woodworking
Show in October. Andrew Forrest and Bruce
Campbell have indicated that they are
committed to seeing that the competition
continues. The executive has agreed to support
the competition. Further volunteers will be
needed to make sure that the competition is a

More Ways to Volunteer!
Art Liestman
As an organization of volunteers, we always
have more participation opportunities!
Our illustrious newsletter editor Amie Hillaby is
taking a brief break to do some serious
travelling. As a result, we will need some help
in putting out the next few newsletters until she
returns. Amie is adamant about not wanting to
give up the job permanently, though. If you’d
like to help with the next few newsletters and
perhaps even earn a permanent spot on the team,
please let me know.
One of the downsides to having very full
monthly meetings is that we don’t have much
time to socialize or to get to know each other
better. It has been suggested that we should
have a picnic in the spring or early summer in
addition to our regular meetings. If you would
like to organize such an event – or find other
ways for members to socialize – please, let
someone on the executive know.
We are now beginning to plan for special events
(such as Bonnie Klein’s visit) for next year. If
you would like to participate in organizing these
events or in suggesting names, we could use
your help. Please let me know if you’d like to
be included in a special event committee.
Many of our members are new to woodturning.
Following in the footsteps of several other
clubs, we would like to institute a mentor
system where more experienced members can
help the less experienced. If you’d like to be a
mentor, please let me know and we’ll put you
on a list in the next newsletter. If you’d like to
be a mentee (pause for laughter), let me know
what you need from your mentor.
